en.title: Milk at one
en.oneLiner: Short answer: around 12 months, infant formula’s job is done. Move her to whole cow’s milk plus food, not to another formula; toddler (“stage 3”) formula isn’t needed. Switch gradually over about 4 weeks, in a cup. Cow’s milk itself isn’t required, it’s just the easiest option. From one, food is the meal; milk is a drink.

labels.planHint: Formula and bottles out, whole milk and cups in. Faster or slower is fine.

bigThree.title: Formula’s job is done at 12 months
lines: Around 12 months, she can move from infant formula to whole cow’s milk plus food (AAP).
Toddler or “stage 3” formula isn’t needed (AAP, WHO). Whole milk does the same job for less money, without added sugar.
Cow’s milk isn’t magic either: it’s just the easiest source of calcium, protein and vitamin D. Yogurt and cheese count too.

bigThree.title: Why wait until 12 months
bigThree.sub: By then, food becomes the meal
lines: Before 1, cow’s milk is hard on the kidneys and gut, is low in iron, and can cause tiny blood loss in poop, which can lead to anemia.
By 1, she gets most nutrition from food. Milk becomes a drink with meals, not the meal.
Yogurt and cheese in her food are fine before 1.
Want a preview? After 11 months, a 1-oz sip of whole milk in a cup lets her try the taste (CHOP).

refs.label: IntermountainParents: “12 - 18 months old: Introduction of Whole Milk” (video)

bigThree.title: About 2 cups a day, in a cup
lines: Aim for about 16 oz (2 cups) of whole milk a day. 24 oz is the ceiling.
Too much milk fills her up, so she eats less iron-rich food. That can mean iron-deficiency anemia, and often constipation.
Whole milk (not skim or 1%) until 2. Use 2% only if the pediatrician suggests it.
Cups, not bottles: daytime bottles go first, the bedtime bottle last, all done by about 15–18 months.

how.intro: Formula’s job is done around 12 months. Switch to whole milk gradually over about 4 weeks.
steps: Skip “toddler” or “stage 3” formula. Whole cow’s milk plus food does the job (AAP, WHO).
Always mix prepared formula (made with water as the label says) with whole milk. Never stir powder into cow’s milk.
Change one feed at a time, and move it to a cup at the same time.
Bottles go in order: daytime first, then nap, bedtime last.
Target about 16 oz a day in total, max 24. She’ll drink less than she did formula. That’s normal; food fills the gap.
how.tip: Happy with straight whole milk on day 1? Great, skip the mixing and go straight to cups.

lines: Practice a cup at meals with water or her formula.
After 11 months: an optional sip of whole milk to try the taste.
Buy plain, pasteurized whole milk with vitamin D. Don’t stock up on more formula.
Replace one daytime feed (e.g. lunch) with 1:1 prepared formula + whole milk, in a cup.
Other feeds stay formula in bottles.
Watch her tummy, poop and skin.
Two daytime feeds (e.g. breakfast + lunch) are now 1:1, in cups.
Daytime bottles are done; nap and bedtime stay for now.
Those cups go to 3 parts milk : 1 part formula.
The nap feed moves to a cup (1:1), or skip it if she’s eating well.
Bedtime bottle: still formula for now.
Every cup is whole milk only. Formula is done.
Bedtime bottle switches to whole milk (a few nights of 1:1 first if she fusses).
Move bedtime milk earlier, before tooth-brushing, in a cup.
Or shrink the bedtime bottle by about 1 oz every few nights.
Replace it with a book and a cuddle. Done!

schedule.note: Sick or teething week? Pause, then pick up again.

tips.title: Storage & temperature
lines: Keep whole milk at the back of the fridge, 40°F (4°C) or colder.
Cold milk is fine. Want it warmer? Stand the cup in a bowl of warm water for a few minutes. Never the microwave (hot spots).
Mix formula + milk right before serving. Once she’s drunk from it, toss leftovers within 1 hour.
Prepared formula not yet served: use within 2 hours at room temperature, or refrigerate and use within 24 hours.
Pour small amounts (2–4 oz) and top up. Less waste.

tips.title: Extra formula cans
lines: Opened powder: lid tight, in a cool, dry cupboard (not the fridge). Most need using within about 1 month of opening, so write the date on the lid and check the label.
The 4-week plan is a good way to finish an opened can. Skip the big tubs near the end.
Unopened, unexpired, undamaged cans: many food banks and formula/baby banks accept them. Call first.
Never use formula past its “use by” date.

tips.title: Stage 3 formula (optional)
lines: Not needed: AAP and WHO say whole milk plus food is enough.
China’s national guideline does suggest a suitable toddler formula at 1–2 years. If you or family prefer it, it’s an OK choice, not a must.
If you use it: pick one without added sugar, follow the label, and count it in the same ~16–24 oz (~500 ml) daily total, still in a cup.
Don’t swap it for sweetened “milk drinks” (乳饮料).

quiz.q: Give whole milk (not skim or 1%) from 12 months to 2 years
quiz.why: Fat helps her fast-growing brain. Switch to 2% only if the pediatrician suggests it for weight or family history.

quiz.q: Buy toddler “stage 3” formula so she doesn’t miss nutrients
quiz.why: AAP and WHO: not needed. Whole milk plus varied food is enough; toddler formulas cost more and often have added sugar. (Chinese guidance differs; it’s optional, see “Practical tips”.)

quiz.q: Serve milk in a cup at meals
quiz.why: Cups protect teeth and leave room for food. Aim to be off bottles by about 15–18 months.

quiz.q: Put whole milk in her daytime bottles so nothing changes
quiz.why: Use the switch to move to cups. Sipping from bottles makes it easy to drink too much and skip meals, and it’s hard on teeth.

quiz.q: Let her fall asleep with a bottle of milk
quiz.why: Milk sitting on teeth overnight causes cavities. Milk first, then brush teeth, then book and cuddle.

quiz.q: Mix formula powder into cow’s milk to ease the taste
quiz.why: That makes it too concentrated. Make the formula with water as the label says, then mix it 1:1 with milk.

quiz.q: Save the leftover formula + milk mix in her cup for later
quiz.why: Once she’s drunk from it, toss leftovers within 1 hour, the same rule as formula.

quiz.q: Let her drink as much milk as she wants
quiz.why: Over 24 oz a day can push out iron-rich food and lead to anemia. About 2 cups is plenty.

quiz.q: Use oat or almond milk as her main milk
quiz.why: Most plant milks are low in protein. Unsweetened, fortified soy milk is the only close match; check with the pediatrician first. Skip rice drinks (arsenic).

quiz.q: Warm the milk a little if she refuses it cold
quiz.why: If her formula was warm, slightly warm milk feels more familiar. Use a bowl of warm water, never the microwave.

watch: Hives, swelling, vomiting or trouble breathing after milk: possible allergy. Trouble breathing → call 911; otherwise call the doctor right away.
Blood in her poop, or repeated vomiting with fewer wet diapers.
Ongoing diarrhea, bloating, constipation, or much more spit-up after starting milk.
Pale skin or lips, very tired, or chewing ice, dirt or paper (possible low iron).
Drinking more than 24 oz a day and eating little food.
Refusing all milk and dairy foods for weeks (ask about calcium and vitamin D).
Not gaining weight, or you’re worried about how much she eats.

disagree.title: How much: 16 or 24 oz?
lines: AAP drinks chart: 16 oz (2 cups) a day at 12–24 months.
2019 US expert consensus: 16–24 oz, depending on how much food she eats.
Children’s Health (Dallas) dietitian: 12–16 oz.
China’s childcare feeding guideline: about 500 ml of milk a day.
Everyone agrees: no more than 24 oz.

disagree.title: Toddler formula: US vs China
lines: AAP and WHO: not recommended.
China’s National Health Commission guideline: for formula-fed 1–2-year-olds, a suitable toddler formula is still suggested, plus some fresh milk, yogurt and cheese.
Chinese Nutrition Society: for ages 2–3, prefers growth milk fortified with vitamin D and calcium.
Either way: about 500 ml of dairy a day, plain, not sweet “milk drinks”. Stage 3 is optional.

disagree.title: Whole or 2%?
lines: US: whole for most kids until 2; 2% for some, if the doctor suggests it.
The 2026 US Dietary Guidelines lean toward full-fat dairy.
WHO: not enough evidence to choose, so no recommendation.
AAP’s own sample menu says “whole or 2%”.

disagree.title: Bottle deadline
lines: CHOP: as soon after 1 as possible.
AAP: sometime between 12 and 18 months.
This plan: daytime bottles gone in 2 weeks, the bedtime bottle by about 15–18 months.

disagree.title: Vitamin D dose
lines: US: from age 1, kids need 600 IU a day; give a 400 IU supplement if she drinks under 32 oz of fortified milk.
China: 400 IU (10 μg) a day from birth to 18.

disagree.title: Cow’s milk before 1?
lines: WHO: for formula-fed babies 6–11 months, animal milk is an acceptable alternative (low-certainty evidence; full-fat).
US: wait until 12 months; stay on formula until then.

details.title: Which milk to buy
lines: Whole, pasteurized cow’s milk, vitamin D fortified, plain.
Never raw (unpasteurized) milk.
Can’t do dairy? Unsweetened, fortified soy milk is the closest match; ask the pediatrician. Oat, almond and coconut milks are low in protein. Skip rice drinks.
Skip flavored milks, toddler “milk drinks” and juice.
Lactose-free whole milk is fine if lactose bothers her (true lactose intolerance is uncommon before 3).

refs.label: American Academy of Pediatrics: “Raw Milk: What Parents Should Know | AAP” (video)

details.title: A sample day
details.sub: Adapted from AAP’s menu for a ~21 lb one-year-old
lines: Breakfast: ½ cup iron-fortified cereal or 1 egg, ½ banana, a few strawberries + ½ cup milk
Snack: toast with peanut butter, or yogurt with fruit + water or ½ cup milk
Lunch: ½ sandwich, ½ cup green veggies + ½ cup milk
Snack: cheese cubes or fruit + water or ½ cup milk
Dinner: 2–3 oz meat, ½ cup orange veggies, ½ cup pasta or potato + ½ cup milk
That adds up to about 12–20 oz of milk, all in cups.

details.title: Allergy or intolerance?
lines: Allergy is the immune system: hives, vomiting, blood in poop, trouble breathing.
Already drinking a cow’s-milk-based formula without trouble? A true milk allergy is unlikely; most show up before 1.
Lactose intolerance is digestion: gas, bloating, loose poop. It isn’t dangerous, is uncommon before age 3, and can happen briefly after a stomach bug.
Either way: stop, and call the pediatrician.
